brief.title: Retake on Inferno

facts.text: You play the CT side on Inferno.
The bomb is planted at B; 36 s remain on the bomb timer.
The attackers detonated a smoke in B site 11 s ago.
No one on your team carries a defuse kit.
Your team has no utility left.
Your team is positioned: 3 in CT Spawn.
Two attackers were last seen in Banana 12 to 13 s ago.
One attacker was last seen in Middle 22 s ago with a Dual Berettas.
The position of one attacker is unknown.

actions.label: Split the retake across two entrances

qualifiers.label: Save, but take a trade if an attacker is met
Let one group take information before the other commits
Fake one side and commit through the other
Arrive together on a timed call
Clear the known position with utility first
Move as one stack and keep utility for the defuse
Send one player ahead to probe while the rest follow
Hold back and go for a late defuse

debrief.whyItWorks: Arriving as one group keeps every defender within trade distance, so a single attacker cannot win an isolated duel, and it lets utility and the defuse be covered at the same time. Here, 3 players faced 4 with about 36 seconds left.
debrief.cost: It commits the whole team to one line of approach, which is predictable and gives the attackers time to set up crossfires on it.
debrief.assumption: The remaining time is enough to clear the site and finish the defuse, and the known information is not a fake.
debrief.breaksWhen: The timer runs too short for a defuse after the clear, or the attackers hold two angles that the group cannot clear at once.

evidenceReview.explanation: The timer decides how long any plan can take. Here the timer stood near 36 seconds.
A sighting narrows where contact is likely, but its value falls quickly with age. That sighting was about 12 seconds old.
A sighting narrows where contact is likely, but its value falls quickly with age. That sighting was about 22 seconds old.

debrief.followupReview: The proposed best answer to the new information was: Continue the chosen retake unchanged. Reasoning: an opponent has been eliminated, which favours pressing the advantage instead of changing course.
debrief.strongestAlternative: The closest alternative was to wait for information first, accepting less time on the bomb for a better read on positions.

counterfactual.changedFact: The bomb timer is far shorter than a defuse needs.
counterfactual.effect: No committed retake could finish, and saving the weapons becomes the stronger line.

reveal.principle: On a retake, weigh the seconds a defuse needs against what you actually know: commit while the clock and the numbers support it, and save when they do not.
